_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC §4
protagonist: Priya Nakamura, senior designer of record at Cascadia Hardscape Design & Build

deliverables.text: A 'Ruled Out' polygon reference table: interior-angle tiling check for every regular polygon pentagon through dodecagon, plus the rhombus/kite non-geometric rejection note.
A labeled coordinate-plane diagram: one repeating unit built via translation/reflection/rotation, with direction stated and lines of symmetry marked.
A border-cut worksheet: missing interior angle of the irregular cut piece, plus a vertical-angle pair and a supplementary-angle pair where cut edges cross the border.
A grid-modulus (GCF) calculation: largest identical cut-guide jig size fitting the plaza's length and width with no partial-inch remainder, for both options.
A total installed-cost-per-square-foot table, Option A vs. B, materials/labor/waste broken out and totaled, against the commission's cost cap.

balance.argument_a: Real math backs the rival's bid: ~$16.66/sq ft total installed, well inside the $18.50 target. Zero interior cut waste by construction (hexagon tiles a flat surface alone).
balance.argument_b: Matches the commission's documented historic-match preference, a real stated evaluation factor. The target is explicitly not a hard disqualifier -- but at ~$19.86/sq ft it comes in noticeably over the $18.50 target, a computed finding, not a guess.
balance.margin_basis: Total installed cost per square foot (material x (1+waste) + labor), Option A vs. Option B, computed in cases/plaza-pavers/sensitivity_model.py cost_breakdown() from Appendix D/G figures. Fully disclosed, single-pass formula -- no hidden interior/border blend (fixed 2026-08-12 after a Tier 2 cold-solve/both-sides finding).

derived._note: Computed by cases/plaza-pavers/sensitivity_model.py, cost_breakdown(PARAMS). Revised 2026-08-12 after Tier 2 adversarial QA found the original model used an undisclosed interior/border cost blend and a material-cost basis inconsistent with Appendix D -- both fixed. case-readiness should re-derive independently.

modeling_assumptions.basis: A stated point inside S7's real $2.00-$8.00/sq ft contractor-market range -- toward the upper end, reflecting a branded geometric-shape product rather than a generic rectangular paver.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Directly load-bearing -- see sensitivity_model.py FLEX sweep for the exact stability range under a +/-50% flex.

modeling_assumptions.basis: No manufacturer (Hanover, Western Interlock) publishes public pricing for an octagon+square combination set -- both list 'contact sales.' A multi-SKU, multi-mold commercial product carries a real, standard manufacturing-economics premium over a single-shape field paver. Retuned from an initial 20% (SPEC section 2: that value put the base margin at 19.1%, and a +50% Tier-2 flex broke the 20% cap at 21.4%) down to 10%.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Directly load-bearing -- the single biggest lever in this case. Flexed +/-50% in Tier 2 probe 5: margin ranges 14.8%-17.3%, Option A stays cheaper throughout.

modeling_assumptions.basis: No plan dimensions exist for a fictional plaza. Total area set to match S5's real, comparable-scale civic paver installation; the 200x150 split is an assumed aspect ratio.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Not load-bearing on the $/sq ft metric (a ratio); directly load-bearing on D4's specific GCF answer.

modeling_assumptions.basis: No single public Kessler Plaza budget document exists (fictional). Set between the two options' real computed totals -- above bare material+labor cost, below a premium pattern's total.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Flexed +/-50% in Tier 2 probe 5: does not change which option is cheaper, only which option(s) clear the target.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Waste factor, simple vs. cut pattern
modeling_assumptions.basis: No single citable percentage for this specific split; order-of-magnitude cross-checked against S8's real 20-40% total-cost-increase figure for intricate patterns. Retuned from an initial 12% cut alongside MA1b (same SPEC section 2 reason).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Flexed +/-50% in Tier 2 probe 5 (jointly with MA1b): margin ranges 14.8%-17.3% -- a minor lever, not the dial that decides the case.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Twist (fountain restoration): curved-edge cutting cost growth
modeling_assumptions.value_used: Option A's cut-labor cost +1.5%, Option B's +3.0%
modeling_assumptions.basis: The case gives no fountain radius, so this is not derived from a measurement -- it is a stated scenario assumption that a larger module (Option B's octagon/square) needs proportionally more full-piece replacement per linear foot of curved boundary than a smaller module (Option A's hexagon). Asserted, not proven; a Hero may reasonably argue the opposite (fewer, larger cuts vs. more, smaller cuts).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Directly load-bearing on the twist only, not the base recommendation. Flipping the two percentages reverses which option's gap grows faster under the twist -- a real, disclosed instability in the twist's specific direction, not the base verdict.

cohort_bands.note: Socratic plan and anchor timings run as written in FACILITATOR.md (0:00-45:00). Anchor 1 vote is a real show-of-hands split worth reading; all three deep-conflict threads run.

Anchors 2 and 3 combine into one pass ('what are the two cost legs, and how do we find them'). Run only one deep-conflict thread (two cost legs, one number) at 20:00-30:00. Twist still drops at 15:00. Total runtime ~30 min.

No vote to take at Anchor 1 -- the learner states an initial position instead of a hands-up split. The guide argues the other side directly rather than cold-calling. Skip the deep-conflict threads; go straight from twist-recommit to Close.
